narrative.title: The Blueprint Wire Format for Relay Towers
narrative.scenario: A telecom ops team must snapshot the live relay-tower tree and ship it to a DR site that rebuilds it byte-for-byte. The wire format is theirs to choose — the contract only demands that every tower, gap, and branch position survives the trip: encode the structure into one string, and later decode that string back into the identical tree.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the preorder serialization — comma-separated node values with the literal token N for every missing child, e.g. '1,2,N,N,3,N,N'.
constraints: The format must round-trip: deserialize(serialize(tree)) reproduces the exact tree

testCases.explanation: Preorder walks 1, its full left wing 2-4-5 with null bookends, then 3 and its right child 6.
The root's missing left child is recorded as N before the right spine 2-3 is unrolled.

hintLevels: Level 1: Nulls carry structure — a format that records every missing child can be rebuilt without guessing.
Level 2: Preorder plus explicit null tokens is self-delimiting: each token completes exactly one subtree slot.
Level 3: Deserialize by consuming tokens in the same order serialization produced them — recursion mirrors recursion.
